title.title: Critical SK dynamics across the temperature transition
title.subtitle: Claim: Glauber dynamics for the SK spin glass has a dimension-free spectral gap for every $\beta < 1$

beats.text: Glauber dynamics: the sampler everyone uses, and SK is where it should break down
Fast mixing was proved only for $\beta < 1/4$. Claim: the whole high-temperature phase
At $\beta = 1$ mixing slows to $n^{2/3+o(1)}$; past it, stretched-exponential traps

sources.quote: Eldan, Koehler & Zeitouni (PTRF 2021) spectral gap for β<1/4
at β=1 worst-start mixing time n^{2/3+o(1)}
for β>1 a stretched-exponential obstruction at time exp(n^{1/10000})
Lean (docs/227.md) covers: the β<1 Poincaré inequality; ratio cutoff only for β<1/2
The universal autocorrelation limits are unformalized.
each of whom read the catalogue summary, every abstract, and the introduction and main theorem statements of every principal manuscript in their group

plain: A computer flips one tiny magnet at a time to sample a spin glass: how fast does it forget where it started?

voice.text: Spin glass dynamics at the transition.
The standard sampler flips one spin at a time.
Fast mixing was known only for beta below one quarter.
Claimed: fast mixing for every beta below one, and slowdowns beyond.
